findings.title: Two more places where the repository's tests and test doubles disagree with the library source, and neither changes who can move funds
findings.difference: None. The disagreements are between files of this repository and hold on every network.
findings.mechanism: This extends F-006 with what a replay of test/libraries, test/Tick.t.sol, test/types and the test doubles in src/test found. First, test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:73-83 expects SafeCastOverflow from Pool.modifyLiquidity only when a token amount is above 2^128 - 1. The variable is named maxInt128InTypeU256 and holds Constants.MAX_UINT128. The source casts both amounts to int128: Pool.sol:212-235 takes the signed results of SqrtPriceMath.sol:261-288 and SafeCast.toInt128 (SafeCast.sol:40-43) reverts once the amount of an add is above 2^127. For amounts from 2^127 + 1 to 2^128 - 1 the source reverts and the test expects success. One case from the replay: spacing 32767, price 735853766953812733719635225319847024411115828962 (tick 873548), range -131068 to 98301, liquidity 2300850342447660200206975412810193765, which is below the per tick cap 6076470837873901133274546561281575204. The amount of currency1 is 313585663563401618519606321096647269736 and the source reverts with SafeCastOverflow. Out of 400,000 random parameter sets 346 fell in this window. Every other outcome, including the order of the eight revert conditions at Pool.t.sol:51-70, matched the source. Second, src/test/SqrtPriceMathEchidnaTest.sol:144-197 asserts that the signed helpers return a positive amount for positive liquidity and a non-positive amount for negative liquidity. The source returns minus the rounded up amount for positive liquidity and the rounded down amount for negative liquidity (SqrtPriceMath.sol:266-270 and 283-287). On 200,000 random inputs the assertion for positive liquidity fails 135,655 times and the one for negative liquidity 48,354 times as written, and every other invariant of that file holds. The forge tests use the sign of the source: a negative delta is owed by the caller (PoolManager.sol:183 and 368-378), and test/libraries/StateLibrary.t.sol:300-301 negates the delta of an add to get the amount paid. The echidna harness is not part of forge test, so nothing in the repository runs it. Third, a correction to the fourth item of F-006: test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:135-158 calls swap for a nonzero amount only when it expects a revert. It makes no call for a valid limit and no call when a zeroForOne limit equals MIN_SQRT_PRICE, so that file says nothing about the boundary that Pool.sol:328-330 rejects and contains no successful nonzero swap. The third item of F-006 was replayed: 8,795 of 120,000 random cases had a zero amount with a 100 percent swap fee, where Pool.t.sol:129-131 expects InvalidFeeForExactOut and Pool.sol:311-320 returns a zero delta without touching state.
findings.impact: None on funds. In the first case the source refuses an add that the test would let through, so it is stricter than the test. A removal whose amount is 2^127 or more reverts at the same cast and has to be split, which an earlier cleared item on the int128 casts already covers. In the second case the source sign is the one the accounting in PoolManager needs: with the sign of the echidna file an add would credit the caller.
findings.preconditions: None. No account gains anything from these disagreements.
findings.mitigations: Change the bound at test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:73 to the int128 maximum and bring the sign assertions in src/test/SqrtPriceMathEchidnaTest.sol in line with SqrtPriceMath, so that the tests and the harness can serve as a reference for the source.

sources.supports: The test expects SafeCastOverflow only above Constants.MAX_UINT128.
Both amounts of a liquidity change are cast with toInt128.
toInt128(int256) reverts when the value does not fit in int128.
The echidna harness asserts a positive amount for positive liquidity.
The signed helpers return a negative amount for positive liquidity, rounded up, and a positive amount for negative liquidity, rounded down.
The swap fuzz test calls swap for nonzero amounts only when it expects a revert.
The forge tests treat the delta of an add as negative.

cleared.check: TickMath: replay of every vector and boundary in test/libraries/TickMath.t.sol by a Python transcription with EVM word semantics, and recomputation of every constant from its definition.
cleared.result: The source reproduces all of it. getSqrtPriceAtTick returns 4295128739 at -887272, 4295343490 at -887271, 1461373636630004318706518188784493106690254656249 at 887271 and 1461446703485210103287273052203988822378723970342 at 887272, and reverts with InvalidTick for 887273, -887273 and the int24 minimum. getTickAtSqrtPrice reverts with InvalidSqrtPrice at MIN_SQRT_PRICE - 1 and at MAX_SQRT_PRICE and returns -887272, -887271 and 887271 for the four listed prices. The 20 per bit multipliers equal 2^128 divided by sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i), rounded to the nearest integer, when computed with 200 digit decimals. The factor 255738958999603826347141 equals 2^64 times the base sqrt(1.0001) logarithm of 2, rounded. The four relations of the fuzz test at TickMath.t.sol:205-223 hold for every one of the 1,774,544 ticks from -887272 to 887271, checked exhaustively, and prices rise strictly from tick to tick. On 20,047 sampled ticks the largest relative error against the exact value is 2.2e-10. The two tests that call a JavaScript reference pass against exact decimal values. The constants and the 14 log steps were also extracted from the file text by pattern and compared with the transcription, so the replay ran the text as written.

cleared.check: SqrtPriceMath and SwapMath: replay of every concrete expectation and revert selector in test/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.t.sol and test/libraries/SwapMath.t.sol, the test constants, and the invariants stated in src/test/SqrtPriceMathEchidnaTest.sol.
cleared.result: All vectors reproduce. Examples: getNextSqrtPriceFromInput gives 87150978765690771352898345369 and 72025602285694852357767227579 for 0.1 ether in at liquidity 1 ether, 624999999995069620 for 2^100 in, and 1 for the maximum inputs; getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput gives 88031291682515930659493278152 and 71305346262837903834189555302 and reverts with PriceOverflow for 4 and 5 out and with NotEnoughLiquidity for 262144 and 262145 out at price 20282409603651670423947251286016; getAmount0Delta gives 90909090909090910 rounded up and one less rounded down; getAmount1Delta gives 100000000000000000. The four literal selectors in assembly (0xf5c787f1, 0x4323a555, 0x4f2461b8, 0x00bfc921) match the keccak of the error signatures. The twelve SQRT_PRICE constants in test/utils/Constants.sol equal floor(sqrt(A/B) * 2^96). computeSwapStep reproduces all nine fixed cases, for example amountIn 9975124224178055, amountOut 9925619580021728 and fee 5988667735148 for the capped one for zero step, and (26215, 0, 79) and (1, 26214, 1) for the two low liquidity cases. The properties of test_fuzz_computeSwapStep held on 243,936 random inputs with no violation, and getSqrtPriceTarget matched its test on 300,000. The echidna invariants held on 200,000 random inputs: an input never buys more than the rounded up amount it pays for, an output never exceeds the rounded down amount, getAmount1Delta equals the exact quotient rounded in the stated direction, and getAmount0Delta equals the full precision formula whenever that formula does not overflow. The only assertions that fail are the sign assertions recorded under F-006.

cleared.check: FullMath, UnsafeMath and BitMath: replay of test/libraries/FullMath.t.sol, UnsafeMath.t.sol and BitMath.t.sol, with exact big integer arithmetic as the reference.
cleared.result: mulDiv and mulDivRoundingUp equal floor and ceiling of a*b/d on 600,000 random triples that include the edge denominators 1, 2, 3, 2^128 - 1, 2^128, 2^128 + 1, 2^255, 2^256 - 2 and 2^256 - 1, and they revert exactly when the denominator is zero or the result does not fit in 256 bits. The two listed inputs whose rounded up result overflows revert. mostSignificantBit and leastSignificantBit are correct for all 256 powers of two, for all 32,640 pairs of set bits and for 400,000 random values, and both revert for zero. divRoundingUp and simpleMulDiv match their tests, including a zero divisor returning zero.

cleared.check: TickBitmap: replay of test/libraries/TickBitmap.t.sol, and the range of the unchecked int24 products in nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord for every tick spacing that PoolManager.initialize accepts.
cleared.result: All 19 fixed expectations of the search reproduce with the nine ticks that setUp flips (the loop at TickBitmap.t.sol:22 stops before 535), for example (84, true) from 78 upward, (511, false) from 255 upward, (-200, true) from -257 upward and (-512, false) from -257 downward. compress, position, flipTick with its TickMisaligned arguments, and both fuzz tests of the search held on 300,000, 100,000, 200,000 and 300,000 random inputs. For every spacing from 1 to 32767 and every reachable tick the product stays inside int24: the extremes are -8,388,352 and 8,355,585 against a range of -8,388,608 to 8,388,607. The first wrap appears at spacing 32769. I ran one sequence with a spacing above the cap to see what the cap prevents: the search result wraps to a positive tick, the clamp at Pool.sol:354-356 turns it into MAX_TICK, computeSwapStep takes its direction from the two prices (SwapMath.sol:60) and moves the price from the bottom of the range to the top at zero liquidity, and the same swap then crosses the same position again and is paid its currency1 a second time. The cap at PoolManager.sol:119 with MAX_TICK_SPACING equal to the int16 maximum (TickMath.sol:28) is the only thing that excludes this, it is enforced on the one path that creates a pool, and the spacing is part of the pool id, so it cannot change later. test/PoolManagerInitialize.t.sol:290-292 expects the revert at 32768.

cleared.check: Tick bookkeeping in Pool: replay of test/Tick.t.sol and of the modifyLiquidity and tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick tests in test/libraries/Pool.t.sol.
cleared.result: tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick returns the seven listed values, among them 191757530477355301479181766273477 for spacing 1, 1917559095893846719543856547154045 for 10, 11505354575363080317263139282924270 for 60, 38345995821606768476828330790147420 for 200 and 6076470837873901133274546561281575204 for 32767. For all 32,767 spacings the cap times the number of usable ticks is at most 2^128 - 1 and the cap is never above the value of the reference formula in Pool.t.sol:173-181. getFeeGrowthInside reproduces the seven cases including the wrap case (16, 13). updateTick reproduces the flip, net and parsing cases, and on 300,000 random states it agrees with the reference contract whenever the reference does not revert. The 737 cases where the source succeeds and the reference reverts all have a delta equal to the int128 minimum, which the test itself excludes. That delta cannot reach a pool: it needs a tick whose gross liquidity is 2^127 or more, and the largest per tick cap is 6.08e36. The revert order of Pool.modifyLiquidity matched Pool.t.sol:51-70 on 400,000 random parameter sets apart from the cast window recorded under F-006.

cleared.check: Position, SafeCast, LiquidityMath, LPFeeLibrary and ProtocolFeeLibrary: replay of their test files.
cleared.result: Position.update reverts with CannotUpdateEmptyPosition and SafeCastOverflow exactly where test/libraries/Position.t.sol:39-59 expects, stores the new fee growth values, and pays (growth difference * old liquidity) / 2^128 on 200,000 random inputs. The assembly of calculatePositionKey hashes the same 58 bytes as abi.encodePacked(owner, tickLower, tickUpper, salt) on 2,000 random inputs, checked with an independent keccak. The six SafeCast functions revert at the bounds the tests list. addDelta equals x + y exactly when the sum fits in uint128 and reverts with SafeCastOverflow otherwise, including (0, -1), (2^127 - 1, int128 minimum) and (2^128 - 1, 1), and returns 0 for (2^127, int128 minimum). isDynamicFee is true only for 0x800000; getInitialLPFee returns 0 for that value, the fee itself up to 1000000 and reverts with LPFeeTooLarge above it, including 0x800001. getZeroForOneFee, getOneForZeroFee and isValidProtocolFee match their tests for all 16,777,216 values of the packed fee. calculateSwapFee equals protocolFee + lpFee * (1000000 - protocolFee) / 1000000 rounded up for every protocol fee from 0 to 1000 against about 3,300 LP fees each, and gives 3997 for (1000, 3000) and 1000000 for (1000, 1000000).

cleared.check: Hooks, CustomRevert, the transient slot libraries, PoolId and the types in src/types: replay of test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol, Lock.t.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.t.sol, PoolId.t.sol, test/CurrencyReserves.t.sol and test/types.
cleared.result: The 14 flags are distinct single bits that sum to 0x3fff, and the example in the comment at Hooks.sol:17-18 (0x2400) decodes to beforeInitialize and afterAddLiquidity. isValidHookAddress returns what the tests list for all 18 literal addresses and for a return delta flag without its action flag. validateHookPermissions pairs each permission with the flag of the same name. bubbleUpAndRevertWith produces byte for byte the ABI encoding of WrappedError(address,bytes4,bytes,bytes) for revert data of 0, 4, 31, 32, 33 and 100 bytes, which is what Hooks.t.sol:1007-1045 and Currency.t.sol:126-180 expect. The four transient slot constants equal keccak256 of Unlocked, ReservesOf, Currency and NonzeroDeltaCount minus one. The literal selectors 0xd4d8f3e6, 0x93dafdf1 and 0xa9059cbb match TickMisaligned(int24,int24), SafeCastOverflow() and transfer(address,uint256). BalanceDelta packing, addition and subtraction match the tests on 300,000 random quadruples and revert exactly when a half leaves int128. Slot0 setters and getters round trip in both orders on 200,000 random values and never write above bit 231. The expectations in test/types/Currency.t.sol follow from Currency.sol:40-118 as read: a token call that reverts with no data gives WrappedError with an empty reason and ERC20TransferFailed, and a failed native send gives selector zero and NativeTransferFailed.

cleared.check: Whole swaps: replay of the concrete swap results in test/libraries/StateLibrary.t.sol and of the swap events and constants in test/DynamicFees.t.sol, test/PoolManager.t.sol and test/CustomAccounting.t.sol through a transcription of Pool.swap, Pool.modifyLiquidity, Pool.donate and Position.update.
cleared.result: Every number reproduces. With 10,000 ether of liquidity on -60 to 60 and on -600 to 600 at fee 3000 and spacing 60, an exact input of 100 ether of currency0 ends at price 78680104762184586858280382455 and tick -139 after three steps, and feeGrowthOutside0 of tick -60 is 3076214778951936192155253373200636 (StateLibrary.t.sol:39-57 and 333-358). A 10 ether swap gives fee growth of 10 ether * 0.003 * 2^128 / liquidity in the input currency only. With 1e18 of liquidity on -120 to 120 the events are (-100, 98, 79228162514264329749955861424, tick -1) for fees 3000, 123 and 1123, (-100, 49, 79228162514264333632135824623) and (-202, 100, 79228162514264329670727698909) at 50 percent, (-100, 0, unchanged price, tick -1) at 100 percent, (-10, 8, 79228162514264336880490487708) at fee 100, and InvalidFeeForExactOut for an exact output at 100 percent. The tick of -1 at an unchanged price follows from the first step, which starts on the boundary of tick 0 and moves the tick without moving the price. A donation of 100 and 200 gives fee growth 34028236692093846346337 and 68056473384187692692674. The protocol fee property of DynamicFees.t.sol:284-316 held on 54,428 random swaps, and the property of StateLibrary.t.sol:294-331 on 3,000 random positions.

cleared.check: Solvency of the transcribed pool math under random sequences of adds, removals, swaps with and without protocol fees, and donations, for spacings 1, 2, 10, 60, 200, 3466, 9973 and 32767 and LP fees from 0 to 100 percent.
cleared.result: In 9,200 random sequences of up to 40 operations the pool never owed more of either currency than it had received, at no step and after every position was removed, with accrued protocol fees set aside. After the unwind the in range liquidity was zero, no tick record remained and every bitmap word was zero. A swap never paid out on its input side. Two unwinds reverted on a full removal with SafeCastOverflow. In both the position held 1e24 of liquidity and the price had moved so far that one amount owed to the owner was above 2^127, for example 187458844526417154903613165193767364960 base units of currency1. The same position came out in two halves of 93729422263208577451806582596883682480 each, so this is the int128 cast limit that an earlier cleared item describes and needs token amounts above 1.7e38 base units. This repeats an earlier cleared item with an independent transcription and adds the 100 percent fee and the largest spacing.

cleared.check: Gas snapshots in snapshots/ as a second witness for the library code paths. forge and solc are not installed, so no value was recomputed. The check is whether each recorded value fits the class and number of storage operations and the count of full precision divisions on the path the source takes.
cleared.result: Nothing in the library snapshots contradicts the source, and several values confirm a path. StateLibraryTest: 2375, 4774 and 6949 are one, two and three cold SLOADs plus about 75 gas per extra loop round of Extsload.sol:31-36, and each name has the count that StateLibrary uses: one slot for getSlot0, getLiquidity, getTickBitmap, getTickLiquidity and getPositionLiquidity, two for getFeeGrowthGlobals and getTickFeeGrowthOutside, three for getTickInfo and getPositionInfo. getFeeGrowthInside records 2375, which fits the slot0 read being its last call (StateLibrary.sol:303-309). TickBitmapTest: 22209 is one SSTORE from zero on a cold slot, 5178 and 5109 are one SSTORE on a cold nonzero slot, and the six search values from 2242 to 2287 are one cold SLOAD each. SwapMathTest and SqrtPriceMathTest: the order of the values follows the number and kind of mulDiv calls per branch, for example the exact input step that stops early costs 165 more for zero for one than for one for zero, in line with 539 against 316 for the two branches of getNextSqrtPriceFromInput. TickMathTestTest: 195022 for 100 calls fits 14 log rounds plus a second price computation, which the transcription shows is needed for 90 of the 100 benchmark inputs. The limits of this witness: TestBitMath records 648 for four different calls and 14 or 25 for the first call of a test, and TickTest records 25 three times, so those regions hold almost no library code after optimisation and say nothing about the arithmetic. The values for PoolManager bytecode size and initcode hash could not be recomputed and are raised as a lead.

cleared.check: The test double src/test/ProxyPoolManager.sol puts noDelegateCall on unlock, take, settle, settleFor, mint and burn, and the production PoolManager does not. Is that a gap in the source.
cleared.result: No. The proxy exists to delegatecall into the real manager, and test/NoDelegateCall.t.sol:63-82 expects DelegateCallNotAllowed only from modifyLiquidity, swap and donate, which carry the modifier at PoolManager.sol:148, 190 and 259, as does initialize at line 117. No test expects the modifier on the other functions. A delegatecall into take, settle, mint, burn, clear or unlock runs the manager's code on the storage, transient storage and balance of the calling contract, so it can move only what that contract holds and cannot reach a pool. The proxy also differs from the manager in the position of the Initialize event (ProxyPoolManager.sol:90-94 against PoolManager.sol:136-141), so it is not kept as an exact mirror.

leads.question: Does a build of src/ with the settings in foundry.toml (solc 0.8.26, via_ir, 44444444 optimizer runs, cancun, bytecode_hash none) give a PoolManager runtime of 24009 bytes and the creation code hash 19281018184167079101887460999643277467915809731640262058315305465805214934776 recorded in snapshots/PoolManagerTest.json, and does forge test --isolate reproduce the gas values in snapshots/ without a diff?
leads.why: The creation code hash is the one witness inside the repository that covers every line of src/ at once. A different hash would show that the source text changed after the snapshots were written, and the gas diff would point at the function. This unit could only check the snapshots for plausibility because forge and solc are not installed and nothing may be installed. The check uses only files of this repository.

leads.question: Does test_fuzz_swap in test/libraries/Pool.t.sol pass under the fixed fuzz seed 0x4444 with 1000 runs, or does it reach a zero amountSpecified with a 100 percent swap fee, where line 129 expects InvalidFeeForExactOut and Pool.sol:311-320 returns without a revert?
leads.why: If the committed test fails against the committed source, one of the two was edited after the other, and the comparison operator at Pool.sol:313 would be the place to look. The zero amount path itself changes no state, so the question is about the history of the file and has no direct fund effect.
